class.name: Box3DContactRules
class.brief_description: A data-driven table that overrides Box3D's four solver callbacks -- never-collide pairs, one-way platforms, friction and restitution -- without a script callback.
class.description: Box3D lets an application override four decisions the solver makes about a contact pair: whether the pair collides at all, whether a contact survives pre-solve, and how the two surfaces' friction and restitution mix. [b]All four run on solver worker threads[/b], where a GDScript [Callable] is unsafe in every configuration. So script does not get a callback: script authors [i]data[/i] here, and C++ evaluates that data inside the callbacks. The hot path allocates nothing, takes no lock and touches no Godot object. [codeblock] var rules := Box3DContactRules.new() rules.set_collision_rule(MAT_GHOST, MAT_WALL, false) rules.set_friction_rule(MAT_ICE, MAT_CRATE, 0.0) rules.set_one_way_rule(MAT_PLATFORM, MAT_PLAYER, Vector3.UP, 90.0) world.contact_rules = rules [/codeblock] [b]One key space for all four rule kinds: the user material id[/b] ([member Box3DBody.user_material_id], [member Box3DCollisionShape.user_material_id]). It is the only thing the friction and restitution callbacks receive -- they get no shape and no context at all -- and the filter and pre-solve callbacks can read it back off a shape, so one id space serves everything. Rules are keyed on an [b]unordered pair[/b] of ids, so a pair has exactly one entry however it was authored; only the one-way rule remembers which side was named first. [b]An empty table cannot move the simulation by one bit.[/b] Where no rule applies, the callbacks reproduce Box3D's own answers verbatim -- [code]sqrt(frictionA * frictionB)[/code] and [code]max(restitutionA, restitutionB)[/code], and "collide" for every pair. Installing a table is safe on a scene that has no rules yet. [b]Two of the four kinds need a per-shape opt-in[/b], because Box3D only consults the world callback when at least one shape of the pair has asked for it. Collision rules need [member Box3DCollisionShape.custom_filtering]; one-way rules need [member Box3DCollisionShape.pre_solve_events]. Friction and restitution rules need no flag at all -- the mixing pair runs for every contact. [b]Threading.[/b] Authoring republishes an immutable snapshot that the workers read through one atomic pointer. Every republish first joins any in-flight [member Box3DWorld.async_step], and steps are only ever launched from the main thread, so no callback can be reading the retired table -- rules can be edited between steps with no synchronisation of your own. Rules are immutable for the duration of a step, which is what keeps the simulation deterministic. [member rules] is a serialisable array, so a table round trips through a [code].tres[/code].

method.name: clear_friction_rule
method.description: Drops this pair's friction override, restoring Box3D's [code]sqrt(frictionA * frictionB)[/code]. Other rule kinds on the pair are kept.

method.name: clear_one_way_rule
method.description: Drops this pair's one-way rule; its contacts survive pre-solve again. Other rule kinds on the pair are kept.

method.name: clear_restitution_rule
method.description: Drops this pair's restitution override, restoring Box3D's [code]max(restitutionA, restitutionB)[/code]. Other rule kinds on the pair are kept.

method.name: clear_rule
method.description: Drops every rule kind for one pair at once.

method.name: clear_rules
method.description: Empties the table. The installed callbacks stay installed and answer exactly as Box3D would.

method.name: get_collision_rule
method.description: Whether this pair is allowed to collide. [code]true[/code] for any pair with no collision rule, since absence of a rule means Box3D's default.

method.name: get_mixing_slot
method.description: Which mixing-bank slot this table holds, or [code]-1[/code] when it holds none. Diagnostic only -- nothing needs it to use the feature. Box3D's friction and restitution callbacks take no context object at all, so the only way to tell one table from another inside them is to hand each table its own function. A table with no friction and no restitution rules never claims a slot; see [constant MAX_MIXING_TABLES] for what happens when they run out.

method.name: get_rule
method.description: Every rule authored for one pair, or an empty [Dictionary] when the pair has none. Keys: [code]material_a[/code], [code]material_b[/code], [code]collide[/code], [code]friction[/code], [code]restitution[/code], [code]one_way_axis[/code], [code]one_way_max_angle[/code] and [code]one_way_from[/code]. The mixing keys are absent unless authored, so [code]has("friction")[/code] is how you tell "friction 0" from "no friction rule".

method.name: get_rule_count
method.description: How many material pairs carry at least one rule. A pair with three kinds on it counts once.

method.name: install
method.description: Registers this table's four callbacks on [param world]. Idempotent, and it creates the world if it does not exist yet, exactly as any other world API call does. A world that is destroyed and recreated -- by leaving and re-entering the tree -- loses its callbacks, so re-install after that, or use [member Box3DWorld.contact_rules], which does it for you and is the reason that property exists.

method.name: is_installed
method.description: Whether this table is currently installed on [param world].

method.name: set_collision_rule
method.description: [param collide] [code]false[/code] makes the pair never collide; [code]true[/code] drops the rule. Needs [member Box3DCollisionShape.custom_filtering] on at least one shape of the pair, and note that it also [b]hides the pair from sensor overlaps[/b] -- Box3D consults the same filter callback there.

method.name: set_friction_rule
method.description: Replaces Box3D's [code]sqrt(frictionA * frictionB)[/code] for this pair. Clamped at 0; a mesh contact asserts the mixed value is finite and non-negative. Needs no per-shape flag: the mixing callbacks run for every contact. This is the rule kind that works the moment the table is installed.

method.name: set_one_way_rule
method.description: A one-way platform, with no script in the loop. A contact between the two materials survives only while the contact normal pointing [b]from[/b] [param material_a] [b]towards[/b] [param material_b] lies within [param max_angle_degrees] of [param axis]; otherwise it is dropped for that step. For a platform you can jump up through and then land on, make the platform [param material_a], the passenger [param material_b], [param axis] [constant Vector3.UP] and the angle 90: a passenger resting on top produces a normal pointing up out of the platform (kept), one rising from below produces a normal pointing down (dropped). [param axis] is [b]world space[/b] and is not re-based on either body's transform -- reading a body pose from a worker thread is exactly what this design exists to avoid, so rotating one-way platforms are out of scope. [param max_angle_degrees] is clamped to [code][0, 180][/code]; 180 makes the rule a no-op. [param material_a] equal to [param material_b] is refused, because with one material on both sides there is no way to tell which way round the normal was authored. Needs [member Box3DCollisionShape.pre_solve_events] on at least one shape of the pair.

method.name: set_restitution_rule
method.description: Replaces Box3D's [code]max(restitutionA, restitutionB)[/code] for this pair. Clamped at 0, same assert as [method set_friction_rule], and likewise needs no per-shape flag.

method.name: uninstall
method.description: Restores Box3D's defaults on [param world]: no filter, no pre-solve and the stock mixing functions. [b]Do not leave a shape's [member Box3DCollisionShape.pre_solve_events] on after uninstalling[/b] -- Box3D's continuous-collision path calls the pre-solve callback without a null check, so that flag is only safe on a world that has a rule table installed.

members.member: The whole table as one [Array] of [Dictionary], in canonical pair order and in the shape [method get_rule] returns. This is the serialised form, so a table round trips through a [code].tres[/code]; assigning it replaces every rule at once.

constants.constant: The pair has a friction override ([method set_friction_rule]).
The pair has a restitution override ([method set_restitution_rule]).
The pair has a one-way rule ([method set_one_way_rule]).

How many distinct rule resources can carry friction or restitution rules at the same time, across the whole process. Box3D's mixing callbacks take no context object, so each table needs its own function from a fixed bank. Eight is far past any real scene; a ninth table logs an error and keeps Box3D's default mixing rather than silently answering with another table's rules. Tables with only collision or one-way rules never claim a slot ([method get_mixing_slot]).
